units.function: Embedded-PostgreSQL integration specification for a local CLI operation that pauses every non-archived Routine belonging to one selected company by reading deployment configuration and mutating the database directly.
units.dependencyDirection: The test imports first-party database tables/createDb, the reusable embedded-PostgreSQL harness and disableAllRoutinesInConfig from the CLI. It writes a full local deployment config containing database, storage, logging, auth and secret-provider paths, then queries database state directly.
units.keyDataModels: Company, Agent, Project and Routine with active/paused/archived status; local deployment configuration with PostgreSQL connection string, embedded data/backup/log/storage/master-key paths and deployment exposure.
units.lifecycle: Start isolated PostgreSQL when supported; seed two companies and their Agent/Project/Routine graphs; invoke company-scoped disable-all; count active/paused/archived records; verify the selected company's active Routine pauses while archived and other-company state remain unchanged; teardown data/config/database.
units.testAssessment: On 2026-08-19 the focused Vitest file and its sole test were explicitly skipped because embedded PostgreSQL support was unavailable on this host; CLI no-emit TypeScript passed. The source test strongly specifies company isolation and status preservation, but provides no executed behavioral proof here and omits transaction failure, concurrent Runs/updates, triggers, audit events, authorization, config tampering and recovery/resume behavior.
units.designRationale: Provide an offline/local-trusted administrative safety operation that can halt scheduled automation even when the normal API/control plane is unsuitable, while preserving archived records and reporting exactly what changed.
units.companyOsProblem: Self-hosted Company OS needs break-glass automation shutdown and disaster-recovery operations that remain tenant-safe, reversible and evidentiary even when the primary service is impaired.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE ONLY. Preserve the requirement for a tested break-glass pause-all capability and explicit changed/already-paused/archived counts, but route normal operations through application ports/events. Any offline database repair tool must be separately packaged, authenticated by local operator policy, transactionally fenced, append a tamper-evident recovery receipt when service resumes and never define the canonical domain API.
units.responsibilityConflict: Direct database mutation bypasses the normal human identity, authorization, approval publication, event and audit/evidence paths. Even a safety pause must record which accountable operator invoked it, why, what exact tenant/revision set changed and how scheduled/in-flight work was reconciled.

securityFindings: The operation reads a plaintext database connection string and master-key path from a local config; config permissions, symlinks, path ownership, error redaction and credential lifetime are untested.
Direct database access bypasses service authorization, policy, optimistic concurrency and normal audit/event publication.
No transaction/fencing behavior is tested against concurrent Routine creation/status change or currently executing Runs and triggers.
The fixture uses local_trusted/private configuration, but the function's enforcement of deployment mode/exposure and selected-company operator authority is not proven here.
Only Routine rows are verified; queued schedules, trigger leases, downstream Work and runtime sessions may remain active or inconsistent after a database-only pause.
Because the test was skipped on this host, runtime compatibility, cleanup and isolation remain unverified in the present audit environment.
